Hybrid Degree Centrality

Source: R/centrality-batch65.R
centrality_hybrid_degree.Rd

Hybrid degree centrality (HC; Ma and Ma 2017) blends the degree of a node with its modified local centrality, in a proportion set by the spreading probability \(p\) of the process the ranking is meant for: $$HC(v) = (\beta - p)\,\alpha\,k_v + p\,MLC(v),$$ with \(k_v\) the degree and \(MLC\) the score centrality_mlc returns. A low \(p\) favors the degree and a high \(p\) the wider neighborhood.

Usage

centrality_hybrid_degree(x, ...)

Arguments

x

Network input accepted by centrality.

...

Further arguments to centrality. The measure uses hc_p (the spreading probability, required), hc_alpha (default 1000) and hc_beta (default 0.1).

Value

A named numeric vector with one score per node, in input node order.

Details

The measure is computed on the simple undirected skeleton of the network, so direction, weights, loops and parallel edges are ignored. hc_p must be given: the source varies it between 0.01 and 0.1 and names no default. Without it the measure warns (class cograph_undefined_measure) and returns NA. hc_alpha brings the degree to the scale of the modified local centrality and is 1000 by default, the value the source uses throughout. hc_beta is 0.1 by default; the source tunes it per network between 0.1 and 0.2. With the defaults the degree term dominates on a small network, and the score ranks nodes much like the degree. At hc_beta = hc_p the score is \(p\,MLC\), and above that the degree enters with a negative sign, a case the source does not use. Isolated nodes score 0. The source prints no value of the measure, so the implementation is checked against the definition only. A hc_p outside \([0, 1]\), a negative hc_alpha or a non-finite hc_beta raises a cograph_bad_parameter error. normalized = TRUE divides the scores by their maximum.

References

Ma, Q. and Ma, J. (2017). Identifying and ranking influential spreaders in complex networks with consideration of spreading probability. Physica A: Statistical Mechanics and its Applications, 465, 312-330. doi:10.1016/j.physa.2016.08.041 .

See also

centrality_mlc, centrality_degree, centrality.

Examples

centrality_hybrid_degree(regulation_net, hc_p = 0.05)
#>    Explore       Plan    Monitor      Adapt    Reflect    Discuss Synthesize 
#>     259.45     311.20     362.95     310.85     259.10     259.80     208.40 
#>   Evaluate     Create      Share 
#>     260.50     311.55     260.50
